variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: GitHub collaboration architecture is the system that turns a Git repository into a shared development workflow. It stores immutable source objects and branch references, then coordinates pull requests, reviews, required checks, merges, search, notifications, automation, audit records, and webhooks around that repository truth.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Policy evaluation and reference update must agree on the same heads”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Freeze the candidate
pairs.detail: Resolve the pull request to an exact candidate SHA and read the current protected target head.
pairs.explanation: Resolve the pull request to an exact candidate SHA and read the current protected target head. Do not authorize a moving branch-name pair.

pairs.label: Revalidate evidence
pairs.detail: Check permissions, required reviews, status results for the candidate SHA, mergeability against the target head, and the active protection-policy version.
pairs.explanation: Check permissions, required reviews, status results for the candidate SHA, mergeability against the target head, and the active protection-policy version.

pairs.label: Advance atomically
pairs.detail: Create or verify the merge result, then update the protected reference only when its stored old head still equals the expected target head.
pairs.explanation: Create or verify the merge result, then update the protected reference only when its stored old head still equals the expected target head. Persist the ref-change journal record or outbox intent in the same authoritative operation.

pairs.label: Publish the outcome
pairs.detail: Publish the committed journal record with stable identity.
pairs.explanation: Publish the committed journal record with stable identity. Derived consumers process it asynchronously and can replay without creating another merge.

variants.hint: Give each part the one job only it can do, then rule out the rest. Core invariantA protected branch advances only after policy is revalidated for the exact candidate commit and the expected target head.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Freeze the candidate: Resolve the pull request to an exact candidate SHA and read the current protected target head. Revalidate evidence: Check permissions, required reviews, status results for the candidate SHA, mergeability against the target head, and the active protection-policy version. Advance atomically: Create or verify the merge result, then update the protected reference only when its stored old head still equals the expected target head. Publish the outcome: Publish the committed journal record with stable identity.

variants.prompt: Which state remains authoritative while search, notifications, Actions, and webhooks catch up?
options: The Git object graph and protected references
The latest search index
The webhook delivery log
A pull-request browser cache
variants.explanation: Immutable Git objects and the current protected reference define repository history. The other systems are derived consumers that may converge asynchronously.

Roll back the branch immediately
Block every future merge until the endpoint recovers
Create a second merge commit for the retry
variants.explanation: The external endpoint is outside the repository transaction. The committed branch remains authoritative while delivery retries proceed independently.

variants.prompt: Why should a worker fleet operate below its raw delivery ceiling?
options: To leave capacity for retries, skew, and worker loss
To make every webhook exactly once
To let search own branch history
To avoid storing immutable Git objects
variants.explanation: Raw benchmark throughput is not a safe operating target. Retry bursts, hot repositories, uneven partitions, and failed workers all consume headroom.

variants.prompt: What problem does a subscriber-scoped dead-letter queue solve?
options: It isolates exhausted deliveries for inspection and replay without blocking other consumers
It turns at-least-once delivery into a distributed transaction
It authorizes protected branch updates
It replaces event retention and consumer offsets
variants.explanation: A dead-letter queue bounds repeated failure, preserves replay context, and prevents one destination from stalling search, audit, notifications, or other webhook subscribers.
